Breaking: Thanks and Giving, a Recipe for a Happy Life

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1126 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Abigail Fagan.
  • Thanksgiving has always been my favorite holiday, a sentiment I frequently hear from others.
  • Unlike other holidays, there are no gifts to buy or exchange, no decorations to hang, or costumes to wear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Abigail Fagan.

Thanksgiving has always been my favorite holiday, a sentiment I frequently hear from others.

What makes Thanksgiving so beloved? Its simplicity, I think.

Unlike other holidays, there are no gifts to buy or exchange, no decorations to hang, or costumes to wear. Instead, we gather, connect, give thanks, and eat. Across religious beliefs and family traditions, this day offers an opportunity to sit around a table, prepare and share a meal, and appreciate what is present in our lives.

In a recent development, of course, Thanksgiving holds different meanings and histories for different people. It can also bring grief, loneliness, and family tension. Yet, I wonder whether the enduring appeal reveals something key about our psychological needs and the path to a well-lived life.

The word thanksgiving dates back to the 1530s, when it referred to the act of expressing gratitude. By the 1600s, it became associated with public celebrations of thanks, and later became the American holiday we know today.

Beyond the delicious meal, I believe Thanksgiving offers a recipe for living. The word itself implies action. Thanks is how we appreciate life, and giving is how we participate in it. By giving, we move our gratitude into service. Gratitude changes what we notice, while giving changes what we do with what we notice. Together, they create a powerful practice of recognizing and reciprocating the goodness in our lives.

I think of Thanks+Giving as a prescription in perception, a conscious practice for approaching life with greater grace, generosity, and connection.

In my clinical work and my own life, I see how expectations contribute to emotional suffering. Often, we become attached to how people should behave or feel, how circumstances should unfold, or how life should look. Gratitude offers another perspective. It encourages curiosity and appreciation, even when things are not as expected.

Industry observers note that research increasingly supports the psychological benefits of gratitude. An international study with over 10,000 participants found that even brief gratitude practices produced modest improvements in positive mood and well-being (Coles et al., 2026). In another recent study with 1,240 participants, researchers found that expressing gratitude in supportive relationships improved both emotional well-being and relationship quality (Nelson-Coffey et al., 2026). Maybe the power of gratitude is how little it takes to experience the benefits.

Industry observers note that my daily gratitude practice is a running list of three things I appreciate. Today, I added trees, my friend Josie, and apples. I do not add explanations or further descriptions. Naming something as ordinary as a tree leads me to notice it again and appreciate its qualities, without asking it to do or be more than it is. Children often find wonder in these ordinary gifts, something we can miss amid the responsibilities and distractions of adulthood.

According to recent reports, noticing our gratitude does not necessarily erase grief, disappointment, or longing. We can think of gratitude as expanding our emotional experience, not denying what hurts. For example, we can miss someone while appreciating the moments we shared. We can be worried about tomorrow while finding something beautiful in today. Gratitude can co-exist with other emotions, and direct our momentary focus toward something positive.

I like to remind myself to look for the awe in all, rather than waiting for something extraordinary to call awesome.

It has been revealed that if gratitude allows us to recognize goodness, giving suggests we share it. Giving is both an expression and an extension of gratitude.

Recent findings suggest that another 2026 study examined whether “grateful” people were more likely to engage in generous acts. Drawing on large international samples and field research, the researchers found that people with a disposition toward gratitude were more likely to engage in personally costly actions benefiting others (Lee et al., 2026). Interestingly, temporarily inducing gratitude did not produce the same effect. This suggests that an enduring grateful orientation is more closely associated with generosity than a fleeting moment of appreciation.

Recent findings suggest that we usually think of generosity in terms of money, donations, or charitable work. But giving can also mean attention, compassion, encouragement, time, and presence of mind for both others and ourselves.

Sources indicate that again, simplicity might hold the secret. I remember my daughter, as a young child, finding a tiny flower, and immediately gifting it to me, my husband, or her brother. She found something that inspired awe and without hesitation, she passed it on.

Recent findings suggest that that spontaneous gesture captures the beautiful reciprocity of giving. Without expecting anything in return, we can experience true connection and the satisfaction of contributing to another person’s joy. The recipient receives a gift, and the giver experiences the pleasure of sharing something meaningful.

According to recent reports, this giving can also include ourselves. Resting when we are tired, accepting help, and treating ourselves with kindness and care, are forms of generosity that sustain our capacity to give to others.

Sources indicate that beyond our annual Thanksgiving feast, what if we made time for thanks and giving every day? Imagine pausing throughout the day to ask ourselves two simple questions:.

What can I name that I am grateful for in this moment?

What can I consciously give to myself or others in this moment?

According to recent reports, the answers and actions do not need to be grand. The recipe is remarkably simple: Notice something good. Give something good. Repeat.

It has been revealed that when we make Thanks+Giving a daily practice, we may discover that the joys of living emerge where gratitude, connection, and service meet. It may just be that the secret sauce to a happy life is found in the name of a favorite holiday.

#122034. Can This Supplement Really Fight Inflammation? Here's What Doctors Say.

📅 25 May 2022 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1251 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Menshealth ↗ Open Full Page

Can This Supplement Really Fight Inflammation? Here's What Doctors Say.

📅 25 May 2022 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1251 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that IS THERE ANYTHING NAC can’t do?
  • Recent findings suggest that N-Acetylcysteine, or NAC, in its supplement form, has managed to accumulate a large number of alleged benefits in recent years.
  • That’s a whole lot of responsibility to place on one single supplement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that IS THERE ANYTHING NAC can’t do? Well, if you listen to the supplement industry, no, not really.

Recent findings suggest that N-Acetylcysteine, or NAC, in its supplement form, has managed to accumulate a large number of alleged benefits in recent years. Depending on who you listen to, NAC supplements can allegedly boost your immune system, detoxify your body, improve cognitive function, increase energy levels, slow aging, increase fertility, reduce inflammation, prevent respiratory infections, and decrease oxidative stress.

That’s a whole lot of responsibility to place on one single supplement.

Add that to the fact that NAC is a proven medical treatment for a couple of specific diagnoses, and you have the perfect setup. Supplement companies can extrapolate evidence into claims that go way beyond current scientific evidence. That’s been a blessing and a curse for NAC manufacturers—and a legal headache that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) just made a major move to solve with the proposed creation of a new regulatory category just for NAC.

It has been revealed that the legal maneuvering is complicated and, if finalized, would allow NAC to be considered a supplement but still a medical treatment which technically isn’t allowed—yet. Basically, there’s a lot to unpack here.

So what can NAC supplement do? And what even is NAC? Is it safe? Let’s break it all down.

NAC IS A sulfur-containing compound, a precursor of the amino acid L-cysteine. In medicinal or supplement form, NAC is converted directly into cysteine, which is then used to make and deliver glutathione, a powerful antioxidant that the body uses to scavenge free radicals and manage oxidative stress. (Yes, the body is a complex system.).

Sources indicate that while NAC isn’t found in food, cysteine is readily available in animal proteins, legumes, dairy, nuts and seeds, and some vegetables. Compared to dietary cysteine, NAC supplements are a faster, more stable way of increasing glutathione levels.

NAC supplements are available in powders, capsules, liquids, and tablets. And while NAC has legitimate medical uses, it’s not officially FDA-approved as a supplement as of this second. Of course, this hasn’t stopped the supplement industry from selling it—or influencers from promoting it.

Recent findings suggest that NAC has been in a weird legal gray area for years. Because it’s an actual medical treatment, it technically can’t be classified as a supplement, even though it’s often presented that way.

Recent findings suggest that the FDA’s proposed rule would classify NAC as the first-ever “Dietary Ingredient Not Excluded from the Dietary Supplement Definition.” Basically, it will be allowed to span the categories of supplement and medication, which has never been done before. If finalized, this ruling would “provide for the lawful use of certain ingredients in dietary supplements that would otherwise be excluded from the dietary supplement definition,” per an FDA constituent update.

Sources indicate that the proposed rule would allow products that contain NAC to be lawfully marketed as dietary supplements, as long as they’re not otherwise in violation of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). In theory, this may eventually apply to other supplement-ish ingredients; Right now, this is centered around NAC.

The proposed rule is open for public comment for 60 days. It’s not clear when the FDA when matter a final rule.

This won’t really impact the general public if it’s finalized. Instead, it clears up potential legal concerns surrounding NAC. “This will more formally allow sales of NAC over the counter, without a prescription,” notes Jamie Alan, PharmD, PhD, a professor of pharmacology and toxicology at Michigan State University in East Lansing.

In a recent development, while some members of the MAHA movement have pushed for this, Alan notes it’s also a case of “well, why not.” She explains, “It is generally safe, and I agree with that assessment. It is also being sold as a supplement already so, why not?”.

It has been revealed that alan stresses that this move doesn’t suddenly legitimize all NAC supplements or claims surrounding them. “If you are buying a supplement, you aren’t necessarily guaranteed that the bottle contains what it states it does,” she says. “There really isn’t evidence yet in my opinion that supplementing with NAC as a dietary supplement will be life-changing for the vast majority of people.”.

NAC is the standard treatment for acetaminophen (Tylenol) overdose. High levels of acetaminophen deplete the liver of glutathione, which is required for the body’s detox pathways. If you’re curious about the geeky scientific mechanism: Promptly repleting glutathione by way of an intravenous NAC infusion helps clear the excess metabolites from the overdose and prevent liver damage.

NAC is also a mucolytic, meaning it can break down thick mucus in the respiratory system. (Yum.) While recent research found that NAC may help with with COPD and chronic bronchitis feel less worse, more investigation is needed to clearly establish effects and benefits.

WELL, NOT ALL that much. Other scientific trials have looked at NAC’s effects on conditions including mood and compulsive disorders, Alzheimer’s, Schizophrenia, and chronic pain. Overall, results have been mixed and largely unremarkable. For most of these conditions and disorders, larger-scale clinical trials are still needed.

So while it’s true that research does exist on NAC and wider health benefits, most of the new research trials examining NAC’s effects use doses that are far higher than what the average person would take, and in forms that are not available to the public.

This hasn’t stopped wellness influencers from broadcasting that NAC supplements can help heal whatever ails you.

Many of these influencers argue that because glutathione may reduce oxidative stress, NAC is amazing for longevity and anti-aging. It’s simple, they argue: Because oxidative stress is associated with aging, increasing glutathione with NAC supplements slows biological aging.

Except raising levels of glutathione in the body does not necessarily translate into a desired outcome. Science agrees: There is no long-term human evidence that showing that this suppresses oxidative stress to the level of having a clinically meaningful outcome. Taking NAC for “healthy aging” is more marketing than anything else at this point.

Recent findings suggest that FOR MOST HEALTHY people, NAC supplements appear to be safe in doses between 600 milligrams (mg) to 1800mg per day. However, doses on the higher end of that range may have a higher risk of side effects such as gastrointestinal upset.

Industry observers note that NAC is not recommended for people with clotting disorders. There are also some potential drug interactions between NAC and immunosuppressants, so it’s always a good idea to get a doctor or pharmacist to cross-reference any supplements with the medications you’re taking.

Again, remember that the supplement industry is largely unregulated. Always buy from reputable companies, and look for products that are third-party tested to ensure that what’s on the label is actually what’s in the bottle.

It has been revealed that NAC has some legitimate—and even life-saving—medical uses, and research is constantly evolving. But what the supplements don’t have at this point, is compelling human evidence showing that NAC has any clinically meaningful effects in healthy people.

Abby Langer, RD is the owner of Abby Langer Nutrition, a Toronto-based nutrition consulting and communications company.

She has a master’s degree from American University and lives by the beach.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The fresh Renault Twingo E-Tech is among the most affordable vehicles, electric or gas-powered, starting at just £14,745 in the UK, or under $20,000.
  • Another affordable, practical EV the US will never see.
  • The retro-looking EV went on sale in Europe earlier this year, starting at under €20,000 ($22,000), before government incentives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The fresh Renault Twingo E-Tech is among the most affordable vehicles, electric or gas-powered, starting at just £14,745 in the UK, or under $20,000.

Another affordable, practical EV the US will never see. Renault’s latest Twingo E-Tech is an electric remake of its iconic 1990s city car.

The retro-looking EV went on sale in Europe earlier this year, starting at under €20,000 ($22,000), before government incentives. In places like Germany, it starts at about €13,990 ($15,500), including the €6,000 ($6,600) federal EV grant.

In the UK, Renault revealed that prices for the Twingo E-Tech will start at just £14,745, or about $19,500. That includes the government’s Electric Clean Car Grant (ECG) of £3,750 ($4,900).

At that price, Renault’s new electric car is among the most affordable vehicles available, including gas-powered cars.

Sources indicate that it’s cheaper than the gas-powered Dacia Sandero (£14,765) and BYD’s cheapest EV, the Dolphin Surf (£18,675). Only a few cars are lower-priced, including the Dacia Spring (£11,990) and Leapmotor T03 (£12,995).

Sources indicate that what do you get for the price? At just 3,790 mm (149.2″) long, the electric city car is a bit smaller than the Hyundai Inster and the BYD Dolphin Surf.

For those in the US, that’s even smaller than the first-generation Chevy Bolt EV, which measured 4,145 mm (163.2″) in length.

Despite its compact size, the “cheeky, practical” 5-door city car, as Renault calls it, offers up to 360 liters of boot capacity. It also features independent, sliding 50/50 folding rear seats to haul bigger items like a surfboard.

With up to 50 kW DC fast charging, Renault stated the Twingo E-Tech can charge from 15% to 80% in 28 minutes.

The base Renault Twingo E-Tech Evolution, priced from £14,745 ($19,500), uses a 27.5 kWh LFP battery and an 80 hp (60 kW) motor, delivering up to 163 miles of WLTP range.

The entry-level version features 16″ steel wheels, a 7″ driver display, 10″ navigation screen, and ADAS features, including cruise control and lane-keep assist.

Renault will offer three Twingo E-Tech trims in total. Industry News: Energy Drinks, Stimulant Supplements Linked to Higher Heart Risks in Young Adults

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1366 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • New research suggests that caffeinated energy drinks and stimulant supplements are associated with significantly higher risks of serious heart problems, including cardiac arrest and heart attack in young adults.
  • The findings, to be presented at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 November 6–9 in Chicago, are preliminary and can’t prove that energy drinks cause heart problems.
  • Still, the results highlight concerning cardiovascular effects of these popular products, particularly among adults under 35 who consume them regularly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New research suggests that caffeinated energy drinks and stimulant supplements are associated with significantly higher risks of serious heart problems, including cardiac arrest and heart attack in young adults.

The findings, to be presented at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 November 6–9 in Chicago, are preliminary and can’t prove that energy drinks cause heart problems.

Still, the results highlight concerning cardiovascular effects of these popular products, particularly among adults under 35 who consume them regularly.

“These products are marketed as everyday pick-me-ups and sold next to soda and bottled water, so most people assume they carry no real risk,” study author Sai Samayamanthula, a fourth-year medical student at the University of Virginia School of Medicine in Charlottesville, VA, said in a news release.

“For many healthy people, if these products are consumed occasionally, the risk is probably small. However, individuals who consume energy drinks or other stimulant-containing supplements regularly can promptly exceed the recommended daily limit for caffeine, so it’s key for people to know that there may be a risk of cardiovascular harm with these products,” Samayamanthula continued.

Researchers from the University of Virginia School of Medicine analyzed 28,345 reports submitted to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) between 2017 and 2025.

Of these, 854 involved caffeinated energy drinks or stimulant supplements, while the remaining reports involved non-stimulant products.

Compared with non-stimulant products, cardiac arrest was reported approximately 11 times more often with energy drinks and stimulant supplements. Heart attacks were reported 4.5 times more often, while ventricular arrhythmias and palpitations were reported about four times more frequently.

Nearly 45% of heart-related reports involved adults ages 18 to 34.

Industry observers note that “Our findings support the case for more systematic safety monitoring of caffeine- and stimulant-containing products. In addition, healthcare professionals should remember to ask their younger patients who have palpitations, chest pain or fainting spells if they recently or regularly consume these products,” Samayamanthula noted.

According to recent reports, gregory M. Marcus, MD, professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco School of Medicine, and chair of the 2026 AHA scientific statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease, wasn’t involved in the study, but mentioned the research “raises concerns that products with very high amounts of caffeine may be harmful to the cardiovascular system.”.

“Although there are biological reasons why that connection could be possible, the study does not prove that caffeine products cause these events, because other factors may have influenced the results found in this analysis,” Marcus noted in a news release.

“More research is needed to understand whether these stimulant products are truly responsible for the reported heart-related events.”.

Cheng-Han Chen, MD, board certified interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center in Laguna Hills, CA, said the findings, although concerning, are not surprising. Chen wasn’t involved in the study.

“We know that energy drinks can have significant effects on the cardiovascular system, primarily because of their stimulant properties,” he told Healthline.

“Caffeine can increase blood pressure and heart rate, while other ingredients, such as guarana and taurine, may further contribute to cardiovascular stimulation and increased stress hormone levels. What is particularly concerning is the potential for these products to trigger serious complications, including abnormal heart rhythms, especially in people with underlying cardiovascular conditions.”.

Chen agreed that occasional energy drink consumption is unlikely to have long-term consequences for heart health in most healthy individuals. However, he said that “frequent or excessive consumption can potentially increase the risk of hypertension and cardiac arrhythmias.”.

Industry observers note that an AHA scientific statement published in July 2026 notes that up to 400 milligrams of caffeine daily is generally considered safe for most healthy adults. That’s roughly equivalent to four or five 8-ounce cups of brewed coffee, depending on how it’s prepared.

However, some energy drinks contain up to three times as much caffeine per fluid ounce as brewed coffee.

Certain energy drinks may also contain stimulants, such as guarana, yerba mate, theobromine, synephrine, and yohimbine.

These ingredients may compound caffeine’s effects on the cardiovascular system.

According to recent reports, “Caffeine stimulates the cardiovascular system, primarily by increasing sympathetic nervous system activity. This can cause the heart to beat faster, raise blood pressure, and increase the workload on the heart,” Chen mentioned.

“Energy drinks may contain additional stimulants, such as guarana and taurine, which can further increase blood pressure and stress hormone levels. With excessive consumption, these effects can become more pronounced and potentially interfere with the heart’s normal electrical activity, increasing the risk of abnormal heart rhythms. People with underlying cardiovascular conditions, particularly hypertension or a predisposition to arrhythmias, may be especially vulnerable to these effects.”.

Other research has echoed these concerns. A 2025 review suggests that high-volume energy drink consumption can prolong the heart’s QTc interval, increase blood pressure, and raise heart rate beyond the effects of caffeine alone.

“There is growing concern about the cardiovascular effects of energy drinks and stimulant-containing supplements, particularly among younger adults,” Chen stated.

“One challenge is that younger individuals may not recognize that these products can have significant effects on their heart and blood pressure, especially when consumed frequently or in combination with other caffeinated products.”.

Young adults accounted for a substantial portion of the FDA reports included in the study, highlighting potential cardiovascular concerns for this age group.

It has been revealed that people with existing heart conditions, a history of irregular heart rhythms, or heightened caffeine sensitivity may face additional risks. Those with undiagnosed genetic heart conditions may also be vulnerable.

A 2024 study identified cases of sudden cardiac arrest occurring shortly after energy drink consumption, particularly among people with underlying inherited heart conditions.

“As a cardiologist, I am particularly concerned about people who may have underlying cardiovascular conditions that have not yet been diagnosed,” Chen noted.

“Excessive stimulant intake can potentially trigger symptoms such as palpitations, chest discomfort, and lightheadedness. In susceptible individuals, it may also increase the risk of more serious complications, including abnormal heart rhythms.”.

Additionally, combining energy drinks with strenuous exercise or alcohol may introduce additional cardiovascular risks.

The findings suggest an association between energy drinks, stimulant supplements, and reported cardiovascular events, but they are preliminary and do not establish cause and effect.

The FDA database also relied on voluntary adverse-event reports, meaning some events may never be reported, while others may receive disproportionate attention.

Industry observers note that researchers also do not yet know how many people consumed these products without experiencing any problems. Without this variable, the reports cannot establish actual risk.

Other factors, including underlying health conditions, medications, and lifestyle habits, may also influence the results. More systematic research and controlled clinical trials are needed.

For most healthy adults, consuming up to 400 milligrams of caffeine per day is generally considered safe.

However, Chen noted that individual tolerance for caffeine may vary, and people with underlying cardiovascular conditions, particularly high blood pressure or abnormal heart rhythms, may need to limit or avoid caffeine altogether.

“Energy drinks can vary considerably in their caffeine content and serving sizes,” Chen noted.

In a recent development, “Depending on the product, a single can may contain anywhere from 80 to 300 milligrams of caffeine. This means that consuming even one or two energy drinks can put someone close to or above the recommended daily limit, particularly when combined with coffee, tea, or other caffeinated supplements.”.

Seek emergency medical attention if you experience chest pain, particularly if it’s accompanied by shortness of breath, fainting, or other symptoms of a possible heart attack.

If you live with a heart condition, ask your doctor about your daily caffeine intake to determine whether you need to cut back.

According to Chen, warning signs of excessive stimulant intake may include:.

“Depending on the severity of these symptoms, medical attention may be necessary,” he stated.

Still, most people may not need to give up caffeine entirely. Monitoring your habits could help protect your heart health. This may include:.

In a recent development, “I encourage people to read product labels carefully and be aware of their total daily caffeine consumption,” Chen said. “I particularly recommend that people with underlying cardiovascular conditions avoid energy drinks.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, as first brought to our attention by Great Britain’s Car, Swedish auction manufacturer Klaravik is preparing to sell the entire NEVS Emily GT project.
  • After Saab Automobile closed its doors in 2012 following an ill-fated tie-up with Spyker, a Chinese consortium called National Electric Vehicle Sweden (NEVS) acquired the majority of the remaining assets, including the Trollhättan factory, manufacturing equipment and intellectual property.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So, you think you can run an electric car company? Well, here’s your chance to prove it. An entire electric vehicle development project is heading to auction this month, and it comes with almost everything you need to get started. There's even a connection to one of the automotive industry's most beloved defunct brands: Saab.

In a recent development, as first brought to our attention by Great Britain’s Car, Swedish auction manufacturer Klaravik is preparing to sell the entire NEVS Emily GT project. The auction includes four complete prototype vehicles, a fifth development mule, spare body panels, parts, tools, and engineering drawings. And unlike a typical automotive auction, where you might leave with a single vehicle, the winning bidder gets the entire collection.

A little backstory is helpful here. After Saab Automobile closed its doors in 2012 following an ill-fated tie-up with Spyker, a Chinese consortium called National Electric Vehicle Sweden (NEVS) acquired the majority of the remaining assets, including the Trollhättan factory, manufacturing equipment and intellectual property. However, NEVS was not interested in building a next-generation Saab 9-3 Aero. Instead, they had their sights set on building an electric car future.

Their vision of that was called the Emily GT, envisioned as a sophisticated electric grand touring sedan capable of competing with established luxury EVs. Development began in late 2019, and just 10 months later, the Emily GT rolled out into view. And much like Saabs of the past, the Emily GT had some unique features—the most obvious being its four electric motors, one mounted inside each wheel. Combined, they produced a healthy 490 horsepower.

However, while the power output was healthy, the financial condition of the company was not. NEVS never secured the funding necessary to bring the car into production. The ambitious project remained stuck in the prototype stage, where it’s stayed frozen .

In a recent development, so, do you think you’re the right person to bring it to market? If so—or even if you’d rather just own a very odd automotive dead-end—Klaravik will open online bidding on November 25, with the auction scheduled to conclude December 9. All four completed vehicles and the accompanying development materials are being offered together rather than individually.

Of course, buying the prototypes and engineering materials doesn't automatically give someone a functioning car company or guarantee a path to production. Manufacturing, regulatory approvals, and financing would still present enormous challenges. However, if you do happen to be an ambitious entrepreneur with deep pockets, this could be your chance to revive an electric vehicle that never had the chance to see the light of day.

How to Move From Worrisome What-Ifs to Wondering What-Ifs

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • If you're tired of feeling like you're never quite enough, or that you're never going to get "there" (wherever there is), consider the following questions.
  • Instead of skimming through these questions the way you might read a typical blog post, I'd like to suggest that you wait until you have a quiet moment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

If you're tired of feeling like you're never quite enough, or that you're never going to get "there" (wherever there is), consider the following questions.

Instead of skimming through these questions the way you might read a typical blog post, I'd like to suggest that you wait until you have a quiet moment. Sit or lie down. Read the words silently or out loud, and really consider them. Try them on, the way you might try on a piece of clothing to see how they fit.

Notice what happens inside your body as you read. See if any of these ideas can sink in. If they can't right now, that's OK, too.

Sometimes old programming runs deep and can feel hard to change. With patience and practice, old beliefs can be questioned and updated, and new ways of thinking and being can take root.

So get comfortable, take a slow, deep breath, and consider these possibilities.

What if I remembered that self-critical thoughts aren't necessarily facts, and I didn't have to believe everything I think?

What if I could begin choosing newly introduced thoughts and beliefs that are kinder, more supportive, and actually feel good?

What if I got off my own back, got on my own side, and decided that I am a good person doing the best I can?

What if I remembered that kindness, compassion, and encouragement help people grow, while berating, pressure, and perfectionism often get in the way?

What if my worth didn't depend on how much I accomplished, how productive I was, or how well I did things?

What if I allowed myself to do things imperfectly, and let good enough be good enough?

What if I could let myself be a beginner, make mistakes, change my mind, and learn as I go, rather than expecting myself to get everything right every time?

What if I spent less time living in worst-case scenarios about the future and more time in the present moment?

What if I slowed down, ever so slightly, and sprinkled small moments of conscious breathing and quiet awareness throughout my day?

What if I stepped out of the never-ending race to get somewhere and spent more moments in actual, factual reality?

What if I softened my gaze when I looked at myself and softened my thoughts when I thought about myself?

What if I spent less time comparing myself to others, remembering that I know nothing about what their lives actually feel like on the inside, and instead offered myself more moments of grace?

What if I became curious about what enoughness feels like?

What if I decided that, in this exact moment, I am already enough? I can still do what I'm moved to do, pursue what matters to me, and take care of what needs to be done without staying trapped on the endless treadmill of never-enoughness.

What if I simply noted, Thank you for what I have, kept the welcome mat out, and stayed open to whatever comes next?

What if, just for today, I let myself be enough?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in bear life, as in human life, sometimes you just have to take a leap of faith. A brown bear (Ursus arctos) cub hanging around Anan Creek in Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska learned that this summer. Its mom, Gemini, was crossing the creek, and one cub jumped right in. But this cub? Not so sure. It stood waiting at the water’s edge, before jumping in.

According to recent reports, for this forceful leap into the water, the park rangers have awarded Gemini’s little cub with the 2026 Yeet of Faith Award. For those keeping score at home, Gemini won this year’s helicopter mom award.

“Cubs learn at their own pace, and thanks to amazing recreation sites like Anan, we get to witness their tiny triumphs up close,” the rangers write.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of Southeast Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots for wildlife is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears (Ursus americanus) and eight brown bears like Gemini and her cubs. Similar to their chubby counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to gorge on salmon ahead of the long winter, and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear around Anan Creek has their own habits and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behaviors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A first-of-its-kind international food pyramid, developed by 22 leading nutritionists from Europe, Canada, the United States, and Australia, was published in Advances in Nutrition in September.

This upcoming food pyramid emphasizes plant-based protein sources, cooking with plant-based oils, and healthier sugars and carbohydrates.

It also echoes the traditional food pyramid used in the United States since 1992.

Industry observers note that the new pyramid breaks away from the Trump administration’s updated nutritional guidelines, which are part of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Make America Health Again (MAHA) agenda and prioritize red meat over plants.

In a recent development, the newly introduced pyramid was designed by a research team led by Brigham Young University professor Karen Della Corte. The researchers noted that this is the first international food pyramid that is designed to reflect scientific agreement across multiple countries and cultures.

Della Corte and researchers from the International Carbohydrate Quality Consortium (ICQC), compared dietary guidelines from multiple countries, including:.

They also analyzed evidence from more than 250 scientific publications, while drawing on the EAT-Lancet Planetary Health Diet to identify principles of healthy eating that may be shared.

The newly introduced pyramid highlights three guidelines:.

While the pyramid emphasizes plant-based proteins, it doesn’t exclude animal proteins.

“I find the newly introduced international food pyramid a more practical and aligned approach for the prevention of chronic disease,” remarked Michelle Routhenstein, Preventive Cardiology Dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the creation of the food pyramid.

“The new international food pyramid places greater emphasis on food quality and the importance of building meals around nutrient-dense plant foods, while still allowing room for lean animal proteins such as fish, poultry, eggs, and yogurt,” she added.

Sources indicate that while the new pyramid and the current U.S. dietary guidelines differ in many ways, they also agree on certain factors.

For example, both sets of guidelines discourage added sugars, refined carbs, and highly processed snacks.

According to recent reports, the differences between the two mainly lie in their emphasis on specific sources of protein and fat. For example, the new pyramid prioritizes plant-based proteins, while the U.S. guidelines place greater emphasis on animal proteins, including red meat.

Recent findings suggest that while both sets of recommendations advise limiting saturated fat, the latest pyramid emphasizes unsaturated plant oils, whereas the U.S. guidelines also include butter and beef tallow as cooking fat options.

Industry observers note that routhenstein noted that an important distinction is that this latest pyramid goes beyond simply telling people to eat more protein or fewer carbohydrates. Instead, it encourages people to consider the quality and sources of those nutrients.

However, the main emphasis of both guidelines is encouraging people to eat fewer ultra-processed foods and more natural or “real” foods.

Routhenstein told Healthline that research consistently shows that plant-forward eating patterns, including the Mediterranean and DASH diets, are associated with better cardiovascular health and a lower risk of heart disease.

Plant foods provide fiber, potassium, antioxidants, and other beneficial compounds that can help support healthy cholesterol levels, blood pressure, blood sugar, and blood vessel function.

“This is not to say that protein and fat are unimportant, but their sources matter,” Routhenstein mentioned.

In a statement from BYU, Della Corte shared the following tips for incorporating the latest pyramid’s recommendations into your diet:.

Industry observers note that the pyramid is a framework, not a personalized prescription. If you have questions about your individual nutritional needs, you can speak with your healthcare professional or a licensed dietitian.

“It is notable to recognize that plant-forward does not mean vegan or vegetarian. The amount and sources of animal protein should be considered to ensure they align with an individual’s cardiometabolic goals and lab targets,” Routhenstein noted.

  • Earlier this month, insurer Allstate published the results from its 2026 Thanksgiving Driver Report.
  • The data also demonstrated a similar, though not quite as extreme, pattern on Black Friday, presumably from people unaware there are Black Friday deals online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, thanksgiving is, as Dominic Toretto might put it, all about family—which means it makes for one of the biggest travel weeks of the year in the United States. Typically, that means egregious traffic and delays on the Wednesday before and the Sunday after, whether you’re making your way by plane, train, or automobile. But apparently, Thanksgiving is also a time when many drivers satiate their need for speed.

Earlier this month, insurer Allstate published the results from its 2026 Thanksgiving Driver Report. The insurance tech giant examined data on 44 million trips during Thanksgiving week in 2025, compared with a typical week in November. One major difference was drivers’ willingness to hit the gas pedal on Thursday morning: Allstate found that between 6 a.m. and 9 a.m. on Thanksgiving, the rate of drivers exceeding 80 miles per hour increased to 200 percent above the normal baseline—a tripling of the average—and it stayed at 100 percent above the norm through noon. South Carolina, Newly introduced York, Texas, North Carolina, and Florida indicated the biggest increases in speeding above 80 mph. (Allstate did not break down the percentage of those drivers who were stressed-out dads deliberately choosing to drive early Thanksgiving morning to make good time and receive commendations from others for having the foresight to travel at that less-convenient time.).

The data also demonstrated a similar, though not quite as extreme, pattern on Black Friday, presumably from people unaware there are Black Friday deals online. Allstate found an 80-percent increase above normal for drivers exceeding 80 mph between 6 a.m. and 9 a.m.

Speedy driving, naturally, creates potential safety risks. Allstate estimates that about one-fifth of the drivers exceeding 80 mph were concurrently engaging in at least one other “risky behavior.” About 90 percent of those drivers engaging in risky behavior were using their phones. However, there were some who had better cause to than others; Monday after Thanksgiving produced the highest increase in roadside service calls for the week, running 52 percent above normal.

Recent findings suggest that as one would expect, drivers are also traveling longer distances over Thanksgiving weekend. Per Allstate, the share of trips longer than 100 miles doubles on Wednesday and Thursday, and the average trip on Thanksgiving Day is 40 percent longer than usual. Which also, perhaps, could explain the desire to go fast.

Nearly 3 million pages of military records from the War of 1812 are finally online

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (498 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812.
  • While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the newly introduced documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census.
  • “In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley said in a recent announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The roughly 2.8 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the newly introduced documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley said in a recent announcement.

The somewhat fresh United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

Today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our users have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

The collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets users explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are presently available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

In a recent development, correction 11/20/26 9:30 a.m. EST: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the pension archive contained around 7 million files. This was based on an initial assessment from researchers in 2010. The article has been updated to reflect the more accurate tally.

#122021. 'So No One Told You Life Was Gonna Be This Way'

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (750 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

'So No One Told You Life Was Gonna Be This Way'

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Showing up for friends on their good days is easy.
  • Sources indicate that this month, Marsha Linehan, developer of DBT, died.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Showing up for friends on their good days is easy. You can celebrate their wins and enjoy their happiness. But being there, really being present for friends when they’re having a rough day or when they do dumb things, that can be more challenging. Our friend is upset, so they spend too much money, or they’re worried, so they pull out of something they had to do, or they’re angry, so they break things. How do we validate their emotions without endorsing their choices?

Sources indicate that this month, Marsha Linehan, developer of DBT, died. One of her many contributions to the psychology world was how to validate emotions with precision. She described six levels of how to validate emotions. The aim is to validate with the highest level possible, but different situations will require different levels. At all times, the goal is to help people notice that their emotion is valid and welcome, even if you don’t agree with the behavior that follows. Your friend doesn’t need a lecture after they’ve done something wrong; they want to feel emotionally understood.

It has been revealed that the most basic level is to simply stay awake and pay attention. I say "simply," but in these days of constant distractions, and phones and devices trying to hold our focus, even just being fully present can be a challenge. How can you show your friend that you’re really listening? You can use eye contact, nodding, asking questions, saying "uh-huh," and more.

The second level is accurate reflection. When you paraphrase back what they’ve said, you let them know that you’ve understood what they’re saying, especially the emotion they’re trying to communicate. Do this without criticism or advice, even if you don’t agree with everything they’ve said. Validation isn’t approval of behavior; it’s letting them know that their feelings are welcome.

Level three is reflecting the unarticulated parts. Let them know that you’ve understood even the aspects they haven’t explicitly told you. Name emotions that you’re guessing they’re probably feeling, e.g., "Oh my gosh, you must have been so hurt by him saying that." It doesn’t even matter if you guess the right emotion. If they reply, "Actually, I was more angry than sad," then you still have lots of emotion to validate.

It has been revealed that at the fourth level, you are validating using past history or biology. Letting your friend know that their behavior makes sense based on their life so far. Statements like "After all you’ve been through this year, I get why this would feel so painful" can put context to their uncomfortable emotions. Even if you would have felt differently in the same situation, you are able to validate their emotion because you understand that their road to this point has been different from yours.

Even more powerful than that is normalising the emotion. Letting your friend know that anyone in that situation would probably feel the same way. Saying things like "I get so upset when that happens," or "That’s something that worries me too," or "We all have moments like that." We can normalise the emotion, even when the behavior wasn’t something we agree with. We can understand that when we’re upset, we make choices that aren’t always the most helpful, and the emotion is still valid. Also, you can normalize their emotion without launching into your own similar story; if your friend is upset, they need you to listen to their pain.

Sources indicate that finally, the highest level of validation is radical genuineness. You listen to them describe their experiences, and you respond with genuine emotion. You're not patronising and saying "there, there." Instead, you are moved by their situation, and you care about them. This is demonstrated through words, body language, and emotion.

Validating your friends (or partner or family member) with the highest level of validation that feels appropriate for the situation is what will help you wholeheartedly be there for them when they’re broke, their job’s a joke, or their love life’s DOA.

In a recent development, koerner, K. (2012). Doing dialectical behavior therapy: A practical guide. The Guilford Press.

Linehan, M. M. (1993). Cognitive-behavioral treatment of borderline personality disorder. Guilford Press.

It has been revealed that linehan, M. M. (2020). Building a life worth living: A memoir. Random House.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turn off reality TV and turn on the bald eagle cams. It’s all the drama you need.

Recent findings suggest that when internet-famous bald eagle Shadow seemingly welcomed a mysterious latest female into his nest earlier this week, many fans have questioned the whereabouts of Kaydee. After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

In a recent development, since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Big Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

Photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Major Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

Mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a upcoming partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

As this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a new partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

Breaking: Melissa Joan Hart Explains It All: Hot Flashes, Menopause, and Turning 50

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (945 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that actor Melissa Joan Hart has a vivid memory of her mother standing in front of their open freezer to cool off.
  • Recent findings suggest that “[She’s] only 20 years older than me, so maybe I missed the part where she was going through [menopause], but there was no conversation about it,” Hart told Healthline.
  • Her own perimenopausal symptoms started with night sweats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that actor Melissa Joan Hart has a vivid memory of her mother standing in front of their open freezer to cool off. As a child, she didn’t understand why. Now, as a 50-year-old woman, Hart knows that her mom was experiencing hot flashes.

Recent findings suggest that “[She’s] only 20 years older than me, so maybe I missed the part where she was going through [menopause], but there was no conversation about it,” Hart told Healthline. “I feel like it’s just becoming a hot topic with women, where…the taboo is going away from it now.”.

Her own perimenopausal symptoms started with night sweats.

“[It] was really jarring, and the first few times, you’re not really sure what that was…do I need to turn the air down or what’s going on here?” Hart said.

Over time, she learned that she was experiencing moderate to severe hot flashes, which affect up to 80% of women during the menopause transition and can persist for 7 to 10 years.

Doctors categorize hot flashes as mild, moderate, or severe, said Diana Bitner, MD, OB-GYN, at Corewell Health.

“[So] if they’re mild, it’s a sense of warmth (maybe in the chest, or the neck, or the face). A moderate hot flash is where there’s associated sweating, and a severe hot flash is something that stops you in your tracks, wakes you up from the middle of the night,” Bitner told Healthline.

Hart has mostly experienced hot flashes while home or at her three sons’ activities, and they have yet to interfere with her work. However, according to research, one in three women report moderate to severe challenges in managing their work due to symptoms related to menopause.

“It’s just so sad that about 10% of women leave the workforce due to menopause,” remarked Bitner. “And so it can really affect our ability to perform at these key years of not only institutional memory, but also of earning power, and it can really affect the whole community.”.

Bitner mentioned women should feel empowered to bring up their menopausal symptoms or questions with their doctor.

“[This] is something that was taboo for so long…women didn’t really talk about this, whether it was because of embarrassment, or [they] weren’t sure if anyone was experiencing it,” she said. “[There’s] no reason, in this day and age, we need to suffer through it…it’s something that there are treatment options for.”.

In fact, Bitner said providing specific details about their symptoms, such as how many mild, moderate, or severe hot flashes they’ve experienced over the past week, can help doctors better assess patients’ needs.

Industry observers note that hart looks to discuss treatment options for her hot flashes with her doctor soon. In the last few years, she noted she has put emphasis on her midlife health.

“I just was sick of waking up with aches and pains in general [thinking], ‘is this the rest of my life?’” she mentioned.

She started listening to self-help books in the car while driving her kids around and found ways to put herself first.

Sources indicate that “My kids are a little bit older, so I kind of have that freedom to be able to do that,” she remarked. “[But] along with getting older, comes the menopause, comes that different time in life. And I think it’s a good time to reevaluate [how] our bodies can’t handle what [they] used to handle, and let’s figure it out.”.

Hart has partnered with pharmaceutical tech giant Bayer on its “Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash” campaign, which encourages women to discuss menopause symptoms with their doctors and promotes Lynkuet, a hormone-free prescription medication for moderate to severe hot flashes associated with menopause.

According to recent reports, “It’s called ‘Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash’ campaign because it shouldn’t, because we should be able to push through, and this should be a time in our lives when our kids are getting older, and we’re able to kind of reinvent ourselves,” said Hart. “And I think it’s an exciting time, and it shouldn’t be something that we’re afraid of.”.

She is embracing speaking openly about midlife health.

“I hit 50 this year, and it was, like, a huge milestone, and I think that’s something to be proud of, and not something to shy away from,” she remarked.

Hart also hopes to challenge the longstanding barriers women face in Hollywood as they age, including fewer opportunities for leading roles.

“[I] think we’re seeing that the generation before, and my generation, it feels like we’re pushing those boundaries…and we’re saying, you know, that women at this age have a lot to give, have a lot of information to share, have a lot of stories to tell and experiences and adventures still ahead of us, and, you know, we’re not ready to stop,” Hart mentioned.

In everyday life, Bitner said that while some patients avoid talking about midlife issues like menopause with their doctors, she is seeing more patients who are confident being forthcoming.

As more women talk openly about menopause, she hopes to include men in the conversation, too. In fact, she invites her patients to bring their partners to appointments, so they can gain an understanding of menopause and the experiences their partners face, such as hot flashes, sleep problems, vaginal dryness, and discomfort or pain during intercourse.

It has been revealed that “[Often], there’s, you know, comments that come up [from men who] say, ‘How do I talk about this without getting in trouble?’” said Bitner. “[We] want everyone to join this conversation…it doesn’t have to be just her issue because we know it’s not.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done.

  • The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done. Having just released a new patch - which already included several updates to Challenges and Assignments - Battlefield Studios has gone in and made even more changes.

This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.

The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge. Now, any headshot beyond 75m will count. Recon Expert 3 is another headshot-themed one that’s been updated, and now requires getting headshot kills beyond 125m, rather than the practically impossible beyond 200m that it required previously.

The Rapid Fire 2 Challenge, which required getting kills beyond 50m with Assault Rifles, has been changed so it now tracks anything beyond 40m. The painful ‘Inflict damage under 15m while hip-firing with Assault Rifles’ has been entirely replaced with one that requires - the far more sensible - inflicting damage while in ADS with Assault Rifles.

A couple of Challenges, such as the one that required suppressing enemies with LMGs, and another that wanted you to deal damage to laser-designated vehicles using lock-on weapons, have both been removed.

Industry observers note that the journey to make Challenges and Assignments easier to complete has been a long one. Progression has been one of the key areas of criticism Battlefield 6 received at launch. The glitch encompassed more than just slow player and weapon XP earn rates, it also prevented players from accessing upcoming Training Paths for the various classes, and several of the game's weapons.

Battlefield Studios attacked the problem from multiple angles, initially boosting the XP players and their weapons would earn, before later reducing the requirements of the Challenges themselves. The developer continued to streamline those requirements over multiple patches, including majorly overhauling the system earlier this month.

It seems the studio is more confident than ever in the game, as it recently revealed that Battlefield 6 will be getting its first free trial next week, offering players who do not own the full game access to iconic modes like Conquest, and Breakthrough - though on an unusual selection of maps.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species.
  • According to recent reports, “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, mentioned in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement.
  • Sources indicate that the 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species. Of those, 20 have officially received spiffy new names from conservationists at the New England Aquarium’s Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life. The researchers curate the annual North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog, and attach personable monikers to a select few baleen cetaceans in order to more easily monitor them. This year, it’s time to wave hello to Dodo, Volcano, and Dolly.

According to recent reports, “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, mentioned in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement. “It can be hard to relate to Catalog #5299, but a whale named Nibbles is bound to be memorable.”.

Sources indicate that the 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991). The sister whales have a mother named Fenway (Catalog #2791), who was also named in honor of the Boston Red Sox. Grand Slam earned her new name thanks to her three patches of raised tissue known as callosities that resemble the bases on a baseball field. Meanwhile, Slide received their name due to the curved scar on her back that recalls someone sliding through home plate. Other right whale names this year include Goose, Donegal, and even Gonzo for the beloved Muppet.

“Although the names are intended to help researchers at sea, they also give the general public a better understanding of the individual whales,” added Caroline Mowdy, a spokesperson for Whale and Dolphin Conservation (WDC).

According to recent reports, collaborators at the WDC also created some lighthearted, yearbook-esque biographies for each whale. For example, Dolly (Catalog #4191), whose callosity looks strikingly similar to the late, great country singer’s larger-than-life hair, apparently loves the song, “Jolene.” Then again, who doesn’t?

According to recent reports, “We see these whales and their families grow each year,” mentioned Mowdy. “Knowing them makes the tragedies even more tragic, but it also makes our determination to protect them even stronger.”.

According to recent reports, on Monday, the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium revealed that there are roughly 382 North Atlantic right whales, representing a 1.8 percent drop in population size from the 2024 estimate. Their primary threats remain getting tangled in fishing line and vessel strikes.

However, even amid their struggles, the 2025–2026 right whale calving season saw the most calves born since 2009. A total of 24 calves were born, including a surprising late addition that was spotted in Canada in September.

#122011. Why We Look Away: Examining Our Response to Homelessness

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1092 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Why We Look Away: Examining Our Response to Homelessness

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • “We do not see things as they are, we see things as we are." —Anaïs Nin.
  • We see homeless individuals on street corners begging, with signs asking for help outside grocery stores, in bank kiosks trying to keep warm, and pushing carts with their belongings, to name just a few places.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

“We do not see things as they are, we see things as we are." —Anaïs Nin.

We see homeless individuals on street corners begging, with signs asking for help outside grocery stores, in bank kiosks trying to keep warm, and pushing carts with their belongings, to name just a few places. We see people in line at soup kitchens or awaiting entrance to shelters. Those of us in the mental health field see more and hear more about homelessness than the usual person.

Homelessness is often discussed in terms of economics, housing shortages, mental illness, and addiction. But there is an alternative dimensional way that we might examine this matter: the psychology behind our response to homelessness. What happens inside us when we encounter another person in need and in distress?

There are five different dimensions of our response to homelessness that I would like to discuss.

First, there is the discomfort of witnessing another person suffering or in need of help. There might be sadness, discomfort, helplessness, perhaps guilt for what we might have, and some revulsion. Witnessing another person’s suffering so openly tells us something about what we all experience at some point in our lives, which is human vulnerability. We depend on a sense of stability, security, and predictability in our lives. We have familiar routines, homes we return to, tasks we need to accomplish, friends who support us. Perhaps viewing another in such dire circumstances disrupts our own sense of permanence and predictability. We may look away, move on more promptly, or stare surreptitiously.

Sources indicate that secondly, we may manage discomfort by creating a sort of psychological boundary between the homeless person and us. We might note that these individuals are different from us. Their circumstances, such as severe illness, lengthy unemployment, and exposure to trauma or domestic violence, are difficult to comprehend. This apparent distance might falsely reinforce the idea that our lives are secure. The greater the difference we create between ourselves and homeless people, the less humanity and humility we experience. On the other hand, erecting this boundary provides us with a sense of distance and difference.

Recent findings suggest that thirdly, there are social cues that we all respond to. If one sees others passing a homeless person sitting or standing on the street, we may believe that no response is necessary or that others will help. We look to others around us to determine how to behave. For example, if we arrive for a party and note that all people entering are kissing the host or hostess, we may be more likely to behave the same way. Follow the leader is a lesson we might have been taught that perhaps needs to be unlearned.

According to recent reports, fourthly, perhaps one of the greatest barriers to understanding homelessness is our tendency to be judgmental and make assumptions about people who are homeless. We might make the mistake of assuming mental illness, laziness, or unwillingness to get a job, even if it is menial work. We may blame poor judgment or irresponsible decisions. It is a fundamental attribution error, which is the tendency to explain the behavior of another through personal characteristics rather than circumstances that might have befallen a person.

Stigma creates a social barrier. Once we label someone, we stop seeing them as an individual and more as their label. Their history, personality, relationships, hopes, and dreams become inconsequential to the label we assign someone. For instance, I have often heard practitioners call someone schizophrenic rather than a person with schizophrenia.

The reality is that homelessness is a circumstance, not an identity.

In a recent development, finally, when we are constantly exposed to the homelessness, war, poverty, and violence that are a routine part of our social media today, we may experience what can be best called compassion fatigue. When people feel overwhelmed by the number of problems they are exposed to daily and their inability to do anything about it, they simply turn away. It produces emotional numbing and avoidance. As we travel to and from work each day by walking or driving, or go to the same supermarket and pass the same person on the sidewalk, they, in essence, become part of the landscape of the route.

This same response occurs for caregivers of very ill persons, who might experience an emotional numbing or habituation.

Understanding these five psychological reactions—discomfort, distancing, social conformity, judgment, and compassion fatigue—gives us a way to think about homeless people and their impact on our behaviors.

Awareness is the first step toward choosing a different response. When someone becomes part of the landscape, we stop noticing them altogether. If instead we stop for a moment and examine our own discomfort rather than rushing past, perhaps we can change our responses, if we so choose. Our own unease likely comes from our own sense of vulnerability and lack of predictability in this world.

It has been revealed that this small shift in framing can neutralize the fundamental attribution error and restore personal history to the person. Each person sitting on a sidewalk was once a child, has a birthday, had a family of origin, probably went to school somewhere, and had people in their lives who cared for them.

Breaking the spell of social cues requires a conscious choice. Making brief eye contact, offering a warm greeting, or simply nodding in recognition of another person’s presence counters the invisibility of living on the street or having to beg. It reaffirms their dignity. In some way or another, we all want to be noticed.

Sources indicate that addressing compassion fatigue demands a different balance. We cannot carry the weight of every global crisis or every unhoused person on our shoulders. There is a marked distinction between empathy—feeling someone else’s distress as our own—and compassion, which combines care with a desire to help in some way. When we shift from overwhelmed empathy to compassion, we move away from paralysis to practicality.

Industry observers note that returning to Anaïs Nin’s insight, the way we react to homelessness is ultimately a mirror. When we look away, we are often protecting our own illusion of control and permanence. When we choose to look closer—with humility, curiosity, and basic human kindness—we acknowledge another person’s struggle and reclaim their and our humanity. There is an inner person inside all of us.

It has been revealed that A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road. Moment Energy’s new Nova battery storage system puts those packs to work on commercial sites. And when a pack wears out, it can be swapped without pulling out the whole system.

Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.

Each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power. It has a 2.94 m by 1.80 m (9.7 x 5.9 ft) footprint, and units can be linked together for projects in the tens of megawatt-hours. A site could charge the batteries when electricity is cheaper or when its solar panels are producing more than it needs, then draw on that power when demand spikes or the grid goes down.

Sources indicate that nova can use packs from different EV models, even when those packs have aged at different rates. Moment’s battery management software tracks how each pack is doing. As packs wear out, the company can replace them while leaving the enclosure and concrete pad in place. Moment indicates its pack replacement service could keep a system in service for more than 20 years.

In a recent development, “We see a future where reengineered EV batteries become essential infrastructure for powering businesses and onshoring manufacturing and supply chains. Nova brings that vision to life, combining safety, engineering, and North American manufacturing to deploy the safest and highest-performance batteries ever made: EV batteries to supercharge our aging grid,” remarked Edward Chiang, co-founder and CEO of Moment Energy.

Sources indicate that moment Energy says Nova is the first storage system built from retired EV batteries to earn both UL 1973 certification for the batteries and UL 9540 certification for the complete system. It was also tested under UL 9540A, which looks at how a battery fire can spread. The factory itself is certified under UL 1974, which covers how used batteries are assessed and graded for reuse.

In a recent development, that matters for businesses with limited space. Nova is designed to sit outdoors alongside the buildings it serves. It uses liquid cooling, detects smoke, heat, and flammable gases, and is rated to operate from −13F to 122F (−25C to 50C).

Industry observers note that moment Energy also says an independent review found that Nova meets US federal sourcing restrictions tied to the clean electricity investment tax credit. Those rules are one part of determining whether a project qualifies for the credit.

Orders are open, and Moment Energy expects the first units to ship in Q1 2027 for deployments across North America.
